correctness.rationale: The three pairings and nine cube-root choices per pairing give 27 distinct lines on a smooth cubic, exhausting the geometric lines. A two-supported point belongs to three lines of a single pairing, whereas a point with all four coordinates nonzero belongs to at most one line per pairing; a point with three nonzero coordinates belongs to none. For the first two pairings an intersection at full support requires αδ=βγ. There are 27 such meeting pairs per pair of partitions, and the third partition contains that point exactly in characteristic two (the required cube-root coefficients have the extra sign −1). Thus 81 cross-pair meetings give 81 double points in odd characteristic or 27 triple points in characteristic two, alongside 18 two-supported triple points. In the split case the exhibited skew six satisfy the same test: first-family exponents are equal, second-family exponents differ by one, so no cross-family equality is possible, and within each family both coefficients vary. The split contraction to a degree-nine del Pezzo over a finite field gives total q²+7q+1, and counting line incidences gives both rows. In the nonsplit case any full-support point on a line has its two uniquely forced ratios in the base field, so both roots are 1; a two-supported point has one ratio forced to 1 and the other arbitrary, giving six rational axis triples. The three rational lines meet pairwise at distinct full-support points in odd characteristic, or at a common point in characteristic two. This yields the other two rows using the bijective cube map and total q²+q+1. Checking the zeros in the four regimes gives exactly the stated five prime powers. The two frozen scripts and their tested field ranges were inspected, not executed; the proof is uniform in q.

value.rationale: The arithmetic invariant separates rational point strata on a natural diagonal cubic over every finite extension. In particular the odd nonsplit law distinguishes rational intersections supported by conjugate lines from ordinary intersections of descended lines. That precise incidence data are useful for evaluating the geometric-line arrangement over finite fields and go beyond re-listing rational lines, the known binary geometry or a few small-field values.
